messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran holdout for paperclip-embed-v1 comparing float16 baseline, int8-q, int6-q. Short-query bin (<16 tokens) recall@1: baseline 0.78 -> int8 0.76 -> int6 0.71. recall@5 largely unchanged. dashboard: https://rwd-infra/dashboards/paperclip-onboard
ash: ouch. can you paste the eval command + short query samples?
maria: eval command:
```
PYTHONPATH=./eval python eval_embeddings.py --model paperclip-v1 --quant int6 --holdout ./data/short_queries.json --k 1,5 --batch 128
```

samples: "reset password", "how to change plan", "refund status", "where is my invoice"
ash: thanks. any particular intent cohort worse? support vs product?
maria: mostly support/faq style; english dominant. also slightly worse for queries with punctuation removed.
devon: can you re-run with per-channel quant vs per-tensor? int6 per-channel sometimes recovers nearest-neighbor stability for short contexts. also try asymmetric calibration.
zane: also double-check tokenizer truncation/prefix behavior — short queries are sensitive to whitespace/token offsets. did any preprocessing change between baseline and quant runs?
maria: preprocessing identical AFAIK. used same tokenizer commit sha: a1b2c3d. re-running with per-channel and asymmetric calibration set now. will try a tiny calibration set biased toward short queries (n=512).
infra-bot: deployment note: paperclip-v1-int6 pulled to staging 2025-03-12T09:15Z (ver=2025-03-12-rc2).
ash: can we get UMAP cluster plots for the short-query cohort vs baseline? 2D shift would help decide if space collapsed.
maria: generating UMAP now; posting link when ready.
maria: umap: https://rwd-infra/plots/paperclip/int6_short_umap.png — looks like FAQ-like queries moved slightly away from their baseline cluster.
zane: I see a small cluster drift. next experiments: per-channel int6 + calibration on the short set, and an int6 hybrid: fallback to int8 for queries < 12 tokens.
nash: fallback/canary idea sounds good — minimize user impact while saving cost. :thumbsup:
eng-platform: noted. we can set a canary route that routes short queries to int8 for first 5% of traffic and monitor recall delta + latency/cost.
maria: plan: 1) rerun per-channel int6 with short-query calibration (n=512) 2) re-eval recall@1/5, silhouette, neighbor-stability (idflip) 3) spin canary route to fallback to int8 for <12 tokens if regression persists. I'll upload numbers later today.
nash: thanks — please include a tiny reproducible eval script snippet in the PR so we can replay.
maria: will do, tagging @devon for quant tips and @eng-platform for canary once results are in.
